subject: Mathematics
learning_objectives: Understand multiplication as repeated addition of equal groups
Memorize and recite multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, and 5
Identify multiplication patterns and arrays using visual grids
Solve simple single-step multiplication word problems
introduction: Begin by showing 3 groups of 2 pencils. Ask students: 'How many pencils in each group? How many groups? Let us add: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.' Explain that instead of adding repeatedly, we can multiply: 3 times 2 is 6 (3 x 2 = 6). Multiplication is quick adding of equal groups!
teacher_activity: Arrange physical counters into rows and columns (arrays) on the table.
Write repeated addition on the blackboard and convert it into multiplication sentences (e.g. 4 + 4 + 4 = 3 x 4 = 12).
Lead rhythmic chanting of tables 2, 3, 4, and 5 with clapping patterns.
Demonstrate skip-counting on a 1-50 number chart (e.g., skip by 2s, 3s, 5s).
student_activity: Build arrays using counting stones or bottle caps (e.g., 4 rows of 3 caps).
Skip-count aloud in pairs while jumping on floor tiles.
Write out multiplication facts in grid notebooks.

lesson_steps.title: Warm-up & Repeated Addition Story
lesson_steps.description: Show groups of leaves/stones and illustrate how 4 groups of 3 equals 12.

lesson_steps.title: Introducing the Multiplication Symbol (x)
lesson_steps.description: Explain the multiplication sign (x) as 'groups of' or 'times'.

lesson_steps.title: Exploring Tables 2 and 3 with Arrays
lesson_steps.description: Draw dot grids for 2x and 3x tables and practice skip counting.

lesson_steps.title: Exploring Tables 4 and 5 with Skip Counting
lesson_steps.description: Connect 5x table to the 5 fingers on each hand and clock minutes.

lesson_steps.title: Quick Quiz & Wrap-up
lesson_steps.description: Rapid-fire verbal questions on tables 2 to 5.

classroom_activities.description: Teams run to the blackboard, solve one multiplication fact (e.g., 4 x 5), and hand the chalk to the next teammate.
Students roll two dice (e.g., 3 and 4) and draw a 3x4 grid of squares in their notebook, counting the total.

assessment_questions.question: A bicycle has 2 wheels. How many wheels do 5 bicycles have in total?

homework.title: Multiplication Table Champion
tasks: Write the table of 3 and table of 4 in your notebook neatly.
Count the total number of table legs in your home using multiplication (e.g., 3 tables x 4 legs).
